notes: Table 0 is a single product-level export; prices, tax flag and tax rate are per-row attributes of that product, so the mapping yields one /prices element per SKU with price_list='standard'.

Net price values are rendered with a '$' prefix while the schema currency default is THB and no currency column exists; currency is unresolved from this file (leading symbol only, not a declared code) and should be confirmed rather than assumed, and no FX conversion should be applied.
SKU is detected as int but is a zero-padded identifier (00470001); it must be read as text to preserve leading zeros.
Tax included='No' and Tax rate='5%' are explicit per-row source values (VAT-exclusive, rate 0.05); they are recorded as evidence, not as inferred country conventions.
No date, warehouse/stock, promotion, category, brand, barcode or description columns are present, so /inventory, /promotions, /category, /brand, /barcode and /description have no source in this file.
No pack-size evidence exists; /unit/pack_size should stay null rather than being derived from 'PCS'.

tables.reason: Single flat sheet with one row per item: unique SKU (12/12 distinct, zero-padded codes 00470001..00470012) plus product name, one sales unit, one price list and one net price per row. This is a product master with an embedded single standard price, not a standalone price list, stock or promotion table.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' matches the sku synonym list; 12 distinct values for 12 rows, one per product. Values carry leading zeros (00470001) and must stay text, so the integer type detected by the profiler must not be used.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header matches product_name synonyms; 12 distinct free-text item names ('SIM neutral 1'..'SIM neutral 12'), exactly aligned with SKU. Descriptive text only, no embedded price/unit facts.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit' is a unit.sell synonym; constant value 'PCS' is already a canonical value in the enum_hint (PCS, PACK, BOX, ...), so it can be normalised without guessing a pack size. No pack-size column exists.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list' matches the price.list_name synonyms and the value is the literal 'standard' on all 12 rows, which the contract also uses as the default price_list. Qualifies the price in the same row, i.e. a single /prices element per product.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' is a price.amount synonym and the column is never empty, always numeric and unique per row (1234.56-1356.77). Confidence reduced because the formatted values are prefixed with '$' (e.g. '$1234.56'), a currency marker evidence in the file but not a header-level currency declaration.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' is an explicit vat_included flag and every row reads 'No', so the amount is VAT-exclusive = false. This is explicit source evidence, not a retail assumption; no VAT adjustment of the amount is implied by the contract.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate' is percent-hinted and constant '5%' on all 12 rows, matching vat_rate. Converted as a fraction 0.05, not copied from any convention: the fixture rate is explicit per row and overrides the schema default of 0.07.

clarifications.why: There is no currency column in the export, and the '$' symbol alone cannot determine the currency. The schema default THB is provisional, and no FX conversion should be applied until the source currency is confirmed.
clarifications.question: The Net price amounts are prefixed with '$', which is not an ISO 4217 currency code and could mean USD, SGD, HKD or another dollar currency. Which ISO currency code should /currency use for these prices?

changes_from_draft: /prices/*/price_list now reads the source 'Price list' column (all rows 'standard') instead of a hard-coded constant.
SKU is trimmed and explicitly cast to string so zero-padded identifiers 00470001..00470012 keep their leading zeros.
/prices/*/vat_included now reads the explicit 'Tax included' flag with parse_bool and a false fallback; /prices/*/vat_rate parses the explicit '5%' value to 0.05.
Net price parsing strips the '$' display prefix before numeric parsing; the symbol is not treated as a currency declaration.
/currency is provisionally THB from the contract default, with low confidence and an operator clarification because the '$' prefix is ambiguous.
No inventory, promotion, category, brand, barcode, description, effective-date or pack-size source columns exist, so those targets remain unmapped.
The previously unmatched 'Tax rate' column is now mapped to /prices/*/vat_rate, so no source column is dropped.
